# stats

Host and Cloudflare-project telemetry for one owner. Everything except /health and host ingest sits behind Cloudflare Access. This file describes the read-only API under /api/v1. Everything is JSON except history responses, which are binary frames (see "History frames").

## Authentication

Send a Cloudflare Access token. From a machine logged in with `cf access login`:

    tok=$(cf access token https://stats.17166969.xyz)
    curl -s -H "cf-access-token: $tok" https://stats.17166969.xyz/api/v1/projects

A missing or invalid token answers 401. Errors are `{"error":{"code","message"}}`. Do not call the `/admin/*` routes; they create, rotate, revoke, and purge hosts.

## Projects (Cloudflare Workers and R2)

    GET /api/v1/projects
    GET /api/v1/projects/:id/history?range=1h|6h|24h|7d|90d&kind=worker|routes|durable-objects|r2|probes|collector
    GET /api/v1/projects/:id/history?range=1h&kinds=worker,r2,collector

`/projects` lists each project with its Worker, buckets, probes, and `collector.lastRunAtMs`, `lastSuccessAtMs`, `lastError`, `stale`. Project ids today: stuff, usr-memories, stats. `kinds` replaces `kind` and returns the selected histories as one bundle, decoded `{projectId, histories: {kind: history}}`. History responses carry `ETag`; send `If-None-Match` to receive `304` when no collector run has changed the data.

Decoded, a response for any kind except `collector` is:

    {projectId, range, kind, fromMs, toMs, stepMs, series: [{metric, values}]}

Every `values` array is aligned to `fromMs + i * stepMs` (epoch ms). `null` means no data, never zero. The newest bucket is unsettled for about 45 minutes because analytics rows arrive late.

Metrics:

- worker: `worker.invocations`, `worker.cpuMsSum`, `worker.cpuMsMax`, `worker.status.2xx|3xx|4xx|5xx|other`
- routes: `route.<METHOD path>.invocations` and `route.<METHOD path>.cpuMsSum` for the 15 routes with the most CPU. Ids in paths show as `:id`, and a path level with many distinct values (package names, hashes) shows as `:*`. Series come back busiest first, and the set can change from run to run. Divide the two for per-route average CPU. For `stats` this separates the front Worker (`POST /ingest/v1/batches`) from the Durable Object (`POST /ingest`, `Installation.jsrpc`, `*/5 * * * *`).
- durable-objects (projects that list namespaces; `stats` does): `do.invocations`, `do.errors`, `do.cpuMsSum`, `do.cpuMsMax`, `do.wallMsSum`, all in milliseconds. Prefer these over the Worker series for Durable Object CPU; they have microsecond precision.
- r2, per bucket: `r2.<bucket>.ops.success|userError|other`, `r2.<bucket>.storageBytes`, `r2.<bucket>.objects`
- probes: `probe.<name>.up` (1 or 0), `probe.<name>.ms`

Reading them:

- Average CPU per invocation is `worker.cpuMsSum / worker.invocations` per index. It is CPU time, not latency, and `cpuMsMax` is approximate. There are no quantiles.
- Worker counts are exact counts of logged invocation events; R2, D1, and Durable Object counts come from sampled analytics (`SUM(sampleInterval)`) and move in coarse steps. Do not trust a bucket with under 100 events.
- For the `stats` project, invocations include its Durable Object calls, so one ingest counts twice: once in the front Worker and once in the Durable Object.
- `userError` on R2 is mostly expected 404 traffic.
- `kind=collector` returns `runs: [{atMs, ok, detail, rowsRead, durationMs}]` instead of `series`.

## Hosts (agent telemetry)

    GET /api/v1/hosts
    GET /api/v1/hosts/:hostId/latest
    GET /api/v1/hosts/:hostId/system
    GET /api/v1/hosts/:hostId/history?range=1h|6h|24h|7d|90d&kind=summary|disks|nets|filesystems|block
    GET /api/v1/hosts/:hostId/history?from=<epoch ms>&to=<epoch ms>&kind=...
    GET /api/v1/hosts/:hostId/history?range=1h&kinds=summary,disks,nets

`from` and `to` replace `range` and may span at most 90 days. History is downsampled to at most 900 points and carries `stepMs`. `latest` and `system` answer 404 until the host has reported. `kinds` replaces `kind` and returns the selected histories as one bundle, decoded `{hostId, histories: {kind: history}}`. History responses carry `ETag`; send `If-None-Match` to receive `304` when the source data has not changed.

Data rules: u64 counters and timings arrive as decimal strings. A missing value is absent or `unavailable`, never zero. Rates are computed from monotonic-clock deltas within one boot, and a counter regression is a gap, never a negative rate.

## History frames

Host and project history answers with content type `application/vnd.stats.history.v1`, not JSON: a 16-byte header, a JSON descriptor, then little-endian numeric columns. Send `Accept-Encoding: br, gzip` (`curl --compressed`); the body is compressed on the wire and your client decodes it. Absent cells are missing, never zero. The layout, node shapes, and field names are in [Architecture](/docs/architecture.md#history-frames). Errors are still JSON.

## More

- [Wire protocol](/docs/protocol.md): validation and rate semantics.
- [Architecture](/docs/architecture.md): components, routes, auth, storage, and rollups.

Both are Markdown, served behind the same Access token.
